epitaph: The belt changed hands exactly once in the surviving record: Masato Tanaka won it outright in a 30-man Deadly Draw match at Deadly Draw 2001 (26 January), lastly eliminating Indiana Kidd Jr., and was still champion when the fed's own last title snapshot was taken. No earlier holder or later title change survives.
name: GLW World Heavyweight Title
notes: From the fed's own title-history ledger, current through 31 March 2001.

epitaph: Three reigns across seven weeks: Doc Dean won it in a ten-man battle royal, lost it seven days after the ledger's own next entry to Mark Schrader (who beat an injury-replacement Brian Adias, not Dean himself, by the fed's own footnote), then reclaimed it thirteen days later and was still champion when the record ends.
name: GLW Midwestern Title
notes: From the fed's own title-history ledger, current through 31 March 2001.

epitaph: The busiest belt on file: four reigns in twelve weeks, changing hands between The Headhunters, the Armstrong brothers, The Extremists, and finally Jesse James Armstrong and Ken Shamrock. The title-history ledger has that pairing still champion as of 31 March; the fed's own separate Current Champions page, dated the same day, calls the titles vacant instead — both readings survive, and nothing resolves which is right.
name: GLW World Tag Team Titles
notes: From the fed's own title-history ledger, current through 31 March 2001.

epitaph: Four reigns, one of them lasting a single day: Colorado Kid won a 30-minute, three-falls-to-two Iron Man Match for the belt and lost it the very next night to Flash Flanagan, who was still champion when the record ends.
name: GLW Television Title
notes: From the fed's own title-history ledger, current through 31 March 2001.
